title: 1801 Prairie gains its carved stone cornice, frieze and gable
items: W. W. Kimball's house at 1801 Prairie: a heavy moulded stone cornice now runs under the steep slate roof along Prairie Avenue and 18th Street, as J. W. Taylor's c. 1895 photograph shows. It stands level with the curved bay's cornice, as one course round both, so the main walls rise about 0.8 m higher to meet it.

On the south pavilion, a carved band with a round medallion now sits over the top windows, and the tall stone gable is filled with a carved leafy panel. Their exact carving is a reconstruction; the photograph is too small to read it.
